newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian aluminium smelter start-up postponed.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian aluminium smelter start-up postponed.

text.p: Nigeria's Ikot Abasi 180,000-tonne aluminium smelter will not be able to start production until early 1997 instead of in November as planned, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The aluminium smelter project will now come on stream early next year," the spokesman of Aluminium Smelter Company of Nigeria (ALSCON) said in Lagos.
He said a delay in the dredging of the eastern Imo River was responsible.
It is the second time the smelter project, commissioned in 1990 has been delayed.
The dredging of the Imo River harbour is to enable bigger ships berth there to load products from the plant.

The project is 70 percent owned by the Nigerian government, with the remaining 30 percent shared between the main contractor, Ferrostaal Ag of Germany, and Reynolds International of the United States.
A subsidiary firm, EBE and Reynolds, had been formed by the two foreign technical partners to manage the project for 10 years after production begins.
The ALSCON spokesman said, "The smelter plant is 80 percent constructed. The Nigerian Gas Company is now test-running supply of gas to the plant, which had once posed a major obstacle."
He said the Royal Dutch Shell Group will supply 33 billion cubic feet of gas annually to the smelter's 536-megawatt power plant on completion.
Most of Nigeria's gas output, produced during the pumping of crude oil is flared.
The World Bank has been critical of the project, saying it was ill-conceived and expensive.
But Nigeria says it hopes to earn much-needed hard currency from the plant and that it will also save on imports of ingots and billets for the local aluminium products industry.
